newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.12 pct on dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.12 pct on dollar inflows.

text.p: Brazil's real closed at 1.0406 per greenback in the commercial foreign exchange market, up 0.12 percent, on dollar inflows, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Thursday surplus of $25 million. But dealers believed net dollar flows may have been larger.
Dealers said the market has been following dollar flows, which will determine the value of the local currency in the near term.

The market was divided about when the Central Bank would move again to lower the real-dollar mini-band. Some players were expecting another decline on Friday, while others are looking for a change next week.
The last time the Central Bank lowered the mini-band was on Monday, to between 1.0400 and 1.0450 reais per dollar.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real ended at 1.0458 per dollar, down 0.01 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 1.32 percent to close at 1.120 per greenback due to an increase in the supply of dollars, traders said.
